source: Hatch Atlas (owner, 2026-11-18), kept as recommended in Hatch_Comparison_REV00

patterns.name: Concrete, plain
patterns.use: Mass concrete footings, unreinforced blinding, and gravity retaining walls in section.

patterns.name: Concrete, reinforced
patterns.use: Structural RC slabs, beams, columns, and retaining walls cut in section.

patterns.name: Concrete block, in section
patterns.use: Concrete masonry unit (CMU) inner leaves, partitions, and foundation walls in section.

patterns.name: Stone, cut
patterns.use: Dressed dimension stone, limestone sills, cornices, and ashlar masonry in section.

patterns.name: Hardcore, compacted fill
patterns.use: Crushed stone or brickbat sub-base compacted beneath ground-bearing slabs and paving.

patterns.name: Gravel
patterns.use: Perimeter French drains, capillary break layers, and ballasted flat roofs in section.

patterns.name: Sand
patterns.use: Paving bedding courses, pipe haunching, and mortar sand beds in section.

patterns.name: Timber, end grain (cut across)
patterns.use: Softwood and hardwood joists, studs, rafters, and wall plates cut transversely in section.

patterns.name: Timber, along the grain
patterns.use: Longitudinal timber members, door linings, architraves, and cabinetry cut along the grain.

patterns.name: Plywood and boards
patterns.use: Structural plywood, OSB, MDF, and laminated joinery boards cut in detail section.

patterns.name: Insulation, rigid board
patterns.use: Rigid PIR, EPS, XPS, or wood-fibre thermal insulation boards in cavity walls and roofs.

patterns.name: Steel and metal in section
patterns.use: Rolled steel sections, aluminium mullions, flashings, and bronze hardware in section.

patterns.name: Glass, in section
patterns.use: Architectural float glass, double/triple glazing panes, and balustrades in section.

patterns.name: Plaster and render
patterns.use: Internal gypsum/lime plaster coats and external sand-cement or lime render in section.

patterns.name: Screed and mortar
patterns.use: Cementitious floor screeds, levelling compounds, and thick mortar beds in section.

patterns.name: Stone, random rubble
patterns.use: Uncoursed quarry-dressed fieldstone walls, garden walls, and vernacular plinths.

patterns.name: Clay roof tiles (pantiles), seen from above
patterns.use: Interlocking S-profile clay pantiles and Roman barrel tiles on pitched roofs in plan/elevation.

patterns.name: Metal standing-seam roof
patterns.use: Zinc, copper, aluminium, or coated steel standing-seam roofs and wall cladding at 550 mm centres.

patterns.name: Terrazzo
patterns.use: In-situ or precast marble-chip terrazzo flooring and stair treads in plan.

patterns.name: Lawn and grass, in plan
patterns.use: Turf lawns, meadows, and soft landscape grass areas on site and ground floor plans.

patterns.name: Planting and groundcover, in plan
patterns.use: Shrub beds, herbaceous borders, and ornamental groundcover planting in site plans.

patterns.name: Water, in plan
patterns.use: Reflecting pools, ponds, fountains, canals, and water features in architectural plans.

patterns.name: Rammed earth
patterns.use: Monolithic load-bearing or thermal-mass rammed earth walls showing compacted formwork lifts.

patterns.name: Compressed earth blocks (CEB), in elevation and in section
patterns.use: Stabilized unfired compressed earth block masonry (290 × 90 mm face) showing coursing and cut.
patterns._note: Architectural note: BIM engines normally separate elevation coursing (Model units) from cut section hatching (Paper units). Both are combined here per specification.

patterns.name: Laterite blocks
patterns.use: Quarry-cut vesicular ironstone laterite blocks laid in courses for tropical load-bearing walls.

patterns.name: Adobe and mud brick
patterns.use: Sun-dried earthen bricks laid in thick mud mortar beds for vernacular and passive-solar walls.

patterns.name: Wattle and daub
patterns.use: Timber-frame infill panels of woven hazel/reed laths plastered with clay-straw daub.

patterns.name: Thatch, in elevation
patterns.use: Bundled water reed or combed wheat straw pitched roofs showing overlapping courses.

patterns.name: Breeze blocks / claustra
patterns.use: Open perforated concrete or terracotta brise-soleil screens alternating two geometric motifs.

patterns.name: Cross-laminated timber (CLT) in section
patterns.use: Engineered mass-timber wall and floor panels showing orthogonal alternating lamella layers.

patterns.name: Hempcrete
patterns.use: Cast bio-aggregate hemp-shiv and lime insulating wall infill in section.

patterns.name: Cork board
patterns.use: Expanded agglomerated cork thermal/acoustic insulation boards and cladding panels in section.

patterns.name: Straw bale
patterns.use: Load-bearing or infill compressed cereal straw bales in wall and roof sections.

patterns.name: Bamboo
patterns.use: Structural and screening bamboo poles shown as hollow culm cross-sections and nodal elevation.
patterns._note: Architectural note: Bamboo culm cross-sections (cut) and nodal culm poles (elevation) are drawn side-by-side here; in BIM production, separate into cut and surface styles.

patterns.name: Gabion
patterns.use: Welded steel wire mesh baskets packed with angular quarry stone for retaining walls and plinths.

patterns.name: Green roof
patterns.use: Extensive/intensive vegetated roof build-up showing drainage layer, substrate, and planting.

patterns.name: Timber acoustic slats on a felt backing
patterns.use: Slatted timber wall and ceiling absorbers mounted over recycled PET acoustic felt backing.
